title: What if you attacked the city Archimedes was defending?

experiment.hypothesis: One continuous camera through a single big 3D set (MiloQ-style) holds attention better than cut-based scenes.
facts: Polybius, Histories 8.3-8.7: Marcellus attacked Syracuse's sea walls with 60 quinqueremes; some ships lashed in pairs carried 'sambuca' ladders; Archimedes' engines hit ships at long and short range, small catapults shot through loopholes; a beam with an iron hand on a chain lifted ships by the bow until they stood on their sterns, then dropped them; Marcellus joked Archimedes used his ships to ladle sea water into his cups.

Plutarch, Life of Marcellus 14-19: Romans so terrified that if they saw a rope or piece of wood over the wall they fled; Marcellus called Archimedes a geometrical Briareus using Roman ships like cups; Archimedes killed by a soldier while absorbed in a diagram, against Marcellus' orders.
Livy 24.34 also describes the iron grapnel on a chain.
Rorres & Harris (2001) and the 1999 BBC 'Secrets of Lost Empires' rebuilt working versions; the siege ran 213-212 BC.

lines.text: You're a Roman sailor. And one old man is about to lift your warship clean out of the sea.
Syracuse, two thousand years ago. Rome sends sixty warships at the city's sea walls.
Some are lashed together in pairs, carrying giant ladders to climb the walls.
But Syracuse has Archimedes. The greatest mathematician alive has had years to get ready for you.
Far out, his catapults hit you. Row closer, and smaller ones shoot through holes in the wall.
Then a wooden beam swings out over your head. An iron claw on a chain grabs your bow.
And lifts. Your ship stands on its end. Then he lets go.
Sounds like a legend? Three ancient historians describe it, and modern engineers have built versions that work.
Soon your crewmates are so scared, if they see a rope dangling over the wall, they turn and run.
Your commander jokes that Archimedes is using his ships as cups, to scoop up the sea.
So Rome stops attacking and waits. When the city finally falls, a soldier finds Archimedes in the middle of a maths problem, and kills him. His commander had ordered him spared.
You survived. Archimedes didn't. Comment what you want to know next.
